summary: A credible hands-on option is the Traditional Silver Craft Workshop at Wat Sri Suphan’s Lanna Craft Wisdom Museum in Wua Lai. The Silver Temple Foundation describes guided repoussé work in which visitors make an engraved metal piece, alongside separate live artisan demonstrations. This is an actual craft lesson, unlike browsing or buying silver at Wua Lai’s Saturday market, but practical session details and December availability need direct confirmation.
whyGo: Try repoussé metalworking with local artisans in the historic Wua Lai silversmithing community, rather than only seeing finished work.
The temple’s living craft museum links the technique to local makers and Lanna heritage; the listed hands-on outcome is an engraved metal keepsake.
bestFor: Travellers who want to learn a basic metalworking technique and are comfortable arranging details directly with a temple workshop.
A half-day cultural outing south of Chiang Mai’s Old City, optionally paired with a separate Wua Lai market visit.
skipIf: You need a guaranteed December 2026 time slot, published price, or confirmed English instruction before travelling; none is listed by the operator.
You only want to shop: the Saturday Walking Street is a separate market and does not itself constitute a lesson.
duration: Allow 1–3 hours as a planning range, not a confirmed class duration. A travel blogger describes a past three-hour silversmith class at Wat Sri Suphan; the temple does not publish how long its current workshop takes.
cost: Workshop fee and materials are not published by the temple. Its museum page says admission is free; a travel blogger reported a 50-baht temple entry charge, so confirm any site fee as well as the class price directly. Do not treat older third-party class listings or prices as current.
hours: The temple lists daily opening hours of 06:00–18:00; those are site hours, not a workshop timetable. Ask which dates and times an artisan can teach in December.
bestTime: Book a daytime session directly and allow time for the museum and temple grounds. Saturday can be combined with Wua Lai Walking Street in the evening, but market hours do not indicate class availability.
gettingThere: Lanna Craft Wisdom Museum is within Wat Sri Suphan, 100 Wua Lai Road, about 1 km south of Chiang Mai Gate. The temple suggests a red songthaew, tuk-tuk or Grab; walking from the south side of the Old City is also practical.
booking: No public calendar, checkout, or booking terms are published on the temple’s workshop page. Contact Wat Sri Suphan at +66 61 403 2815 or watsrisuphan@gmail.com and request a confirmed hands-on lesson, date/time, language, duration, group size, total fee and materials. Its page distinguishes hands-on workshop from live demonstration, so specify which you want. No December 2026 dates are confirmed online.
accessibility: The temple’s public information does not describe step-free access, seating, or workshop accommodations; ask before booking. The Silver Ubosot has a traditional restriction barring women from entering, but this concerns that ordination hall; workshop access is not specified. Visitors should cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes before entering buildings.
practicalTips: Get written confirmation that participants will handle tools and make an item; a demonstration or museum visit is not the same class.
Ask whether the metal is silver or another metal, and whether the finished piece and materials are included in the quoted fee.
Keep the workshop appointment separate from silver shopping; Wua Lai’s Saturday market is an evening street market, not a scheduled class.
decemberNotes: No December 2026 workshop schedule or holiday closure notice is published. December is within Chiang Mai’s popular cool season, so confirm a specific class date and operating hours directly before building the day around it. The temple’s daily opening hours do not mean the artisan workshop operates every day.
uncertainties: Current workshop booking channel, December dates, fee, duration, language, capacity, materials and accessibility arrangements remain unpublished.
A travel blog describes a three-hour historical class and links to a third-party booking listing, but that does not verify that the same class or price is bookable now.
The photo is a historical image of a participant doing silverwork at Wat Sri Suphan, as identified by its source; it does not establish the current lesson format. Reuse permission is not established.
